clauses.reason: Section 1 authorizes the Director of Selective Service to prescribe the rules and regulations needed to carry out the Military Selective Service Act, and keeps regulations earlier issued by the President in effect until the Director amends or revokes them. The delegation has no end date or ending condition and nothing held revokes it; the Selective Service System regulations that cite the order as authority (22 hits in the eCFR search) and the U.S. Code note show it in use. The second sentence continues earlier presidential regulations until the Director amends or revokes them; no held source shows when, or whether, every such regulation was replaced, so the claim rests on the delegation in the first sentence, which is a standing authority and not a completable task.

clauses.reason: Section 2(a) requires the Director, before publishing a proposed rule or regulation, to request the views of listed officials and allow at least 10 days for them. It is a standing procedure with no end. Section 15 of EO 12608 (signed September 9, 1987; the held text states no later effective date) substitutes Secretary of Health and Human Services for Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare in the orders it lists, which include EO 11623. Section 60 of EO 13286 (68 FR 10619, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) strikes the Secretary of Transportation and the Department of Transportation in section 2(a) and inserts the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Department of Homeland Security. Before: the list named the Secretary of Transportation (when the Coast Guard is serving under the Department of Transportation); after: it names the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Department of Homeland Security in that place. The substance of the consultation duty is unchanged, so section 2(a) continues as amended.

research_rationale:
EO 11623 (signed October 12, 1971; 36 FR 19963) delegates to the Director of Selective Service the authority to issue rules and regulations under the Military Selective Service Act (section 1) and sets the consultation, referral and publication procedure for those rules (section 2(a) to (c)), with a rule of construction preserving the President's own authority (section 3). I read the complete held Federal Register original; its five dossier clauses match the order's own structure (sections 1, 2(a), 2(b), 2(c) and 3), so the inventory is confirmed without correction. The order has no sunset or ending condition. Two held later orders amend it: EO 12608 section 15 (September 9, 1987; Health and Human Services for Health, Education, and Welfare) and EO 13286 section 60 (effective March 1, 2003; Homeland Security for Transportation in section 2(a)); both are attached as later events on section 2(a) with before and after wording, and the U.S. Code note printing the order lists exactly these two amendments. The dossier also lists EO 12977 as a later event; the text it offers is EO 13286's section 60 under an EO 12977 queue label, and the held text of EO 12977 (60 FR 54411) does not name EO 11623, so EO 12977 is not a later event. The held regulations and notices that cite the order (FR Doc. 94-31721, 95-6288, 04-2427 and 04-8606, and 32 CFR parts 1602, 1605 and 1609 authority lines) apply it and do not end it. The three bounded searches record no revocation or supersession. All five clauses are operative on the original text as amended, checked through 2026-10-14.
